title: Hising up their petticoats,
html_source: Refers back to Mulligan’s ditty about Mary Ann in “Telemachus”.

anchor.prefix:
peech ceases. It flows purling, widely flowing, floating foampool, flower unfurling. 

 Under the upswelling tide he saw the writhing weeds lift languidly and sway reluctant arms,
anchor.suffix: in whispering water swaying and upturning coy silver fronds. Day by day: night by night: 1932#45lifted, flooded and let fall. Lord, they are weary; and, whispered to, they sigh. S
